headline: Service stopping now ends all in-flight watches via closeWatches
summary: When the router service stops, it now calls router.closeWatches() after marking not-ready, which cancels every active watch so the HTTP server's Shutdown does not block on never-idle streaming connections. Clients see their watch end and re-establish it against another replica.
reason: Shutdown path now actively terminates in-flight streaming requests, a runtime lifecycle and concurrency change a reviewer must judge.
focus: closeWatches is safe to call when the router has no entries or was never reconciled, and is idempotent if stopping runs twice
ordering: watches end after SetNotReady, so load balancers stop sending new watches before existing ones are cut
watches started concurrently with or just after closeWatches are also ended rather than leaking and blocking Shutdown
